elements.label: Figure 3.5
elements.title: The number of services offered by national standards bodies falls as countries develop
elements.content:
Chart type: Scatter plot with a negative downward-sloping linear trendline in red.
 y-axis: Number of services offered by national standards body, ranging from 0 to 10.
 x-axis: GDP per capita (US$), on a logarithmic scale ranging from 100 to 100,000.
 Data points: Multiple scatter points distributed across the chart area, showing a general trend that countries with lower GDP per capita tend to have a higher number of services offered by national standards bodies, while countries with higher GDP per capita tend to have fewer services.
Source: WDR 2025 team, based on World Bank and ISO 2025.
Note: The survey sample includes 116 national standards bodies: 13 in low-income countries, 28 in lower-middle-income countries, 34 in upper-middle-income countries, and 41 in high-income countries.
